venue.name: Old Cemeteries Society of Victoria
venue.description: The Old Cemeteries Society of Victoria is a volunteer, non-profit society that researches and preserves Victoria's heritage cemeteries and gives guided walking history tours, mostly at Ross Bay Cemetery on Fairfield Road. School group tours are offered on prepared themes including a general cemetery tour, BC history, the gold rush, Emily Carr and women's history, and the site says they suit Grade 4 and up. Private group tours can be booked any day of the week except Sunday, and themed tours for the general public run every Sunday at 2 pm from mid February to mid December.

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: These wheelchair-accessible walking tours follow the paved pathways.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Groups that come by private bus can drive into Ross Bay Cemetery to meet the guide at a selected location. Vehicles can enter the cemetery only on weekdays, but parking is easily available on nearby streets or at the Fairfield Plaza (1516 Fairfield Road).

venue.hours_notes: The cemetery is open to the public every day of the year during daylight hours. Vehicles can enter the cemetery only on weekdays.
venue.seasonal_notes: Public themed tours run every Sunday at 2 pm from mid February to mid December. Private group tours can be booked on any day of the week except Sunday.

programs.name: School walking history tour
programs.description: A guided walking history tour of Ross Bay Cemetery for a school class or other children's group. Prepared tours include a general tour of the cemetery, a BC history tour, a gold rush tour, an Emily Carr tour and a women's history tour, and the guides will build a tour around a teacher's own topic. The site says the tours suit Grade 4 and up and links them to Art, Drama, English Language Arts and Social Studies. To book, leave a message on the voice mail at 250 598 8870 with the topic, preferred date and time, grade level and group size, or use the form on their school tours page. A teacher's kit and a self guided map are also available for classes coming on their own.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the cemetery with a guide, stopping at graves and monuments while the guide tells the stories of the people buried there.
programs.our_note: The whole visit is outdoors on your feet with nothing to sit on, so plan for weather and shoes. Ask what the $45 covers when you call, because their other group page charges $10 a head instead.
programs.practical_summary: An outdoor walking tour with no washrooms, indoor lunch space or wet weather plan mentioned anywhere on the site. Their tours stay on paved paths and a private bus can drive into the cemetery on weekdays, so ask about drop off when you book.

programs.name: Private group walking tour
programs.description: A cemetery tour booked privately for your own group with one of their guides, on any day of the week except Sunday. Topics include BC history, women's history, gold rushes, BC place names and Victoria street names, and other topics are available. Tours last about an hour and cost $10 per person. The guides wear a portable voice amplifier so everyone can hear, the route follows the paved pathways, and a group arriving by private bus can drive into Ross Bay Cemetery to meet the guide. This page is written for seniors' groups but says the tours are for any private group.
programs.what_children_do: Walk for about an hour along the paved paths with a guide, stopping at graves and monuments to hear the stories behind them.
programs.our_note: This page is written for seniors' groups, so check that the guide will pitch it for children when you call. At $10 a head it works out dearer than their school tour for anything but a very small group.
programs.practical_summary: About an hour outdoors on paved, step free paths, with a guide who wears a voice amplifier so everyone can hear. Washrooms, lunch space and a wet weather plan are not mentioned, so ask when you book.
programs.evidence: Tours last about an hour. The cost is $10 per person.

programs.name: Sunday public walking tour
programs.description: A themed walking history tour open to anyone, every Sunday at 2 pm from mid February to mid December, with a different topic each week. Most are at Ross Bay Cemetery, where the group meets at the cemetery entrance on Fairfield Road opposite the south end of Stannard Street, and some are at other heritage cemeteries in Greater Victoria. No reservations are needed. It costs $5 for non members and $2 for members, paid by cash or e-transfer, and the tours last about an hour. Topics for 2026 range from the gold rush and nursing pioneers to a ghost tour in October and a Christmas tour in December.
programs.what_children_do: Join whoever else has turned up, follow the guide around the cemetery for about an hour and stand and listen at each grave.
programs.our_note: Nobody takes a reservation for these, so a group simply arrives and joins the public. The subject changes every week and none of them is written for children, so check what is on that Sunday before you bring a young group.
programs.practical_summary: No booking needed, you turn up at 2 pm on a Sunday and pay $5 a person for about an hour outdoors. Washrooms, lunch space and a wet weather plan are not mentioned on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: Members pay $2 instead of $5. The fee can be paid by cash or e-transfer.
programs.evidence: Our tours begin at 2 pm. No reservations needed. It costs $5 for non-members and $2 for members.

gaps: Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
No indoor space or shelter is mentioned, and there is nowhere published to eat lunch. The tours are entirely outdoors.
No wet weather policy is published for any tour.
No maximum or minimum group size is published for school tours or private group tours.
How much notice they need to book a school or private tour is not stated.
How many adults have to come with a class is not stated.
How long a school tour lasts is not stated. Private group tours and the Sunday tours are described as about an hour.
Which months school tours are available is not published (unknown).
Whether under fives can join a private group tour is not addressed. Only the school tours page gives an age, Grade 4 and up.
The society has no street address of its own. The address recorded here is Ross Bay Cemetery, 1495 Fairfield Road, taken from their own cemeteries page, because that is where the tours happen.

Their two mailing addresses differ: the contact page gives PO Box 50004, RPO Cook Street, Victoria BC V8V 4Z8, and the Ross Bay brochure page gives Box 50004, #15-1594 Fairfield Rd., Victoria BC V8S 1G1. Neither is a place to visit.
The image tagged for social sharing on the home page is the society logo rather than a photograph, so the hero photo was taken from the school tours page instead.
No coordinates are published on the site, so the location is pending geocoding.
The school tour page carrying the $45 price was last updated in 2024. The $5 and $2 Sunday prices come from the 2026 tour schedule page, which was updated in August 2026.
Booking runs through a voice mail box and a contact form. There is no online booking and no published email specifically for tour bookings, only the society's general address.

conflicts.note: Their school page charges one flat $45 for the whole tour and their private group page charges $10 a person. Which one applies to a class of children is not spelled out. Worth settling when you book, because for 25 children the difference is large.
